items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I came to the whole idea of – Sonny Stitt helped me, like I told you.

ctx.x: How did you come to your understanding of those rhythms?

When I came to – I came to the whole idea of – Sonny Stitt helped me, like I told you. He said, “Time. Time is everything. You got to do it at the right time.” In whatever you do, if you do it at the right time, it’s valuable. If you do it at the wrong time, something that really taken a lot of work to construct it and all that, it’s not valuable. Time is everything. In music, in order for people to really appreciate it, the rhythm that it’s based on is one of the things that can make people from another – that…

In developing that band, was there a kind of a growth phase, so that the persons who were more indoctrinated into 4 could catch up with all the complexities that were going on? We’re not just talking about Cuban rhythms, but you pointed out, we’re talking about Puerto Rican tradition, Colombian tradition, Panamanian tradition, and while there are similarities, there are also profound differences.
